Compliance · US

California Consumer Privacy Act and CCPA regulations

Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, §7000 et seq. (Article 9: §§7120–7124) · statute and regulations as effective 2026-01-01; cybersecurity-audit, risk-assessment and ADMT regulations approved by OAL 2025-09-22 · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: For-profit businesses meeting the CCPA thresholds that collect California residents' personal information; the §7120 audit duty applies to those whose processing presents significant risk (§7120(b)).

Civ. Code §1798.100 General Duties of Businesses that Collect Personal Information
Civ. Code §1798.100(a) Tell consumers, when or before collecting their data, what is collected and why.
Civ. Code §1798.100(a)(1) Notice must list data categories, purposes, and sale or sharing; new uses need fresh notice. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(a)(2) Sensitive data categories, purposes and sale or sharing must be disclosed; incompatible new uses need notice. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(a)(3) State how long each data category is kept, or the criteria; don't exceed necessity. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(b) Third-party collectors may give notice on their homepage, or on-site where collecting physically. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(c) Collection, use, retention and sharing must be necessary, proportionate and compatible with the original purposes. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(d) Sharing or selling data, or giving it to vendors, requires a contract with specified terms.
Civ. Code §1798.100(d)(1) Contract must limit the data's disclosure to specific, limited purposes. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(d)(2) Contract must bind recipient to follow the law and match its privacy protection. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(d)(3) Contract must let the business take reasonable steps to verify proper use of the data. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(d)(4) Contract must require the recipient to warn the business if it can't comply. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(d)(5) Contract must let the business act to halt and fix unauthorised data use. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.100(e) Apply reasonable security measures suited to the data against unauthorised access, destruction, use, modification or disclosure. We detect

arch.privileged-key-client-sideShipping a privileged key to every browser is not a reasonable security practice.

db.rls-missingLeaving a table without row-level security where the rest are protected is not reasonable access security.

db.sensitive-auth-data-storedRetained CVV, track or PIN columns show consumer payment data kept when it should be gone, directly evidencing an unsafe data-protection practice.

db.sensitive-column-plaintextSensitive personal information stored without encryption, hashing or tokenisation is not reasonably secured.

secrets.committedCredentials committed to source code are not a reasonable security practice for systems holding personal information.

secrets.in-historyA credential recoverable from git history is not reasonably secured.

tls.verification-disabledAccepting any certificate exposes personal information in transit, short of reasonable security.
Civ. Code §1798.100(f) Businesses need not reveal trade secrets as defined by regulation. Coming soon

Civ. Code §1798.135 Methods of Limiting Sale, Sharing, and Use of Personal Information and Use of Sensitive Personal Information
Civ. Code §1798.135(a) Businesses selling, sharing, or using sensitive data beyond permitted uses must offer accessible opt-out mechanisms.
Civ. Code §1798.135(a)(1) Homepage needs a prominent titled link letting consumers opt out of sale or sharing. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(a)(2) Homepage needs a prominent titled link letting consumers restrict use of sensitive data. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(a)(3) Business may use one clearly labelled link covering both opt-out and sensitive-data limiting. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(a)(4) If opt-out responses mention a charge, the terms of any financial incentive must be shown. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(1) Honouring browser or platform opt-out preference signals can replace the homepage link duty. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(2) Business honouring signals may link a page where consumers consent to ignoring the signal, under conditions.
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(2)(A) Consent page must let consumers withdraw consent as easily as they gave it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(2)(B) Link to the consent page must not degrade browsing and must look like other links. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(2)(C) Consent page must follow the technical specifications set by regulation. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(b)(3) Business may choose either the homepage-link approach or the signal approach, not both. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c) Introduces obligations for businesses subject to this section.
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(1) Opting out must not require creating an account or giving extra information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(2) Privacy notices must describe opt-out rights and give links or state signal compliance.
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(2)(A) The rights description and links belong in the online privacy policy. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(2)(B) Any California-specific privacy rights description must also carry the rights text and links. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(3) Staff who handle privacy inquiries must be trained on opt-out requirements. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(4) After an opt-out, stop selling or sharing and wait a year before asking again. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(5) For minors under 16 who decline, stop selling and wait a year before re-asking. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(c)(6) Information collected when processing an opt-out may be used only to honour it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(d) A separate California-dedicated homepage with required links can satisfy the homepage duty. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(e) Consumers may authorise others to opt out for them, and businesses must comply. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.135(f) Recipients of a passed-along opt-out may use data only for specified business purposes.

Civ. Code §1798.135(f)(2) Recipient may not retain, use, or disclose the data except in limited ways.

Civ. Code §1798.135(f)(2)(B) No use of the data outside the direct relationship with the business. Coming soon

Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(A) Publicly available information and lawful truthful public-concern information are excluded from personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)(i) Introduces what counts as publicly available.
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)(i)(I) Publicly available includes lawfully released government records. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)(i)(II) Publicly available includes data reasonably believed lawfully made public by the consumer or media. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)(i)(III) Publicly available includes data disclosed by recipients where the consumer set no audience limit. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(2)(B)(ii) Biometric data collected without the consumer's knowledge is never publicly available. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(3) Deidentified and aggregate consumer information fall outside personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(4) Personal information may exist in many formats.
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(4)(A) Personal information formats include paper, printed images, records, and video tapes. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(4)(B) Personal information formats include digital text, image, audio, and video files. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(v)(4)(C) Personal information formats include compressed or encrypted files, metadata, and AI systems that output it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(w) Defines precise geolocation as device data locating a consumer within a 1,850-foot radius. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(x) Defines probabilistic identifier as identifying a consumer or device with better-than-even certainty. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(y) Defines processing as any operation performed on personal information, automated or not. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(z) Defines profiling as automated processing evaluating or predicting personal aspects of a person. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(aa) Defines pseudonymization as processing so data needs separately held extra information to attribute. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab) Defines research as ethical scientific study; reuse of collected data has conditions.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(1) Research use of previously collected data must fit the original collection purpose. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(2) Research data must be pseudonymized and deidentified, or aggregated, so no consumer can be linked. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(3) Research data needs technical safeguards forbidding reidentification except where the research itself requires it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(4) Business processes must expressly forbid reidentifying research data, apart from research needs. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(5) Business processes must guard against accidental release of deidentified research information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(6) Research information must be shielded from any attempt to reidentify it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(7) Research use is limited to purposes consistent with the original collection context. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ab)(8) Researching business adds security controls restricting research data access to those who need it. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ac) Defines security and integrity as a set of abilities listed below.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ac)(1) Defines security as systems detecting incidents harming availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of personal data. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ac)(2) Defines security as businesses detecting incidents, resisting malicious or fraudulent acts, and aiding prosecution. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ac)(3) Defines security as businesses being able to protect people's physical safety. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(1) Defines sale as disclosing personal information to a third party for money or other value. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2) Lists circumstances in which a business is not selling personal information.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2)(A) No sale occurs when the consumer directs the business to act intentionally.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2)(A)(i) Consumer-directed disclosure of personal information is not a sale. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2)(A)(ii) Consumer-directed interaction with third parties is not a sale. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2)(B) Sharing an identifier to signal a consumer's opt-out or limitation is not a sale. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ad)(2)(C) Transferring data in a merger or acquisition is not a sale, with notice duties. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae) Defines sensitive personal information; categories follow.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1) Sensitive information includes personal information revealing the listed categories.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(A) Government identifiers such as social security, licence, state ID or passport numbers are sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(B) Account or card numbers together with access credentials count as sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(C) Precise geolocation is sensitive personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(D) Race, ethnicity, immigration status, religion, philosophy or union membership are sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(E) Contents of mail, email and texts are sensitive unless business is recipient. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(F) Genetic data is sensitive personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(G)
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(G)(i) Neural data is sensitive personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(1)(G)(ii) Defines neural data as nervous system activity measurements not inferred from other data. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(2)
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(2)(A) Biometric processing meant to uniquely identify a consumer is sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(2)(B) Collected and analyzed health information is sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(2)(C) Collected and analyzed sex life or orientation information is sensitive. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ae)(3) Publicly available sensitive information is excluded from sensitive and personal information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(af) Defines services as work, labor and services, including those tied to goods. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(1) Defines service provider as a processor acting under a written contract with prohibitions.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(1)(A) Service provider contract must bar selling or sharing the information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(1)(B) Contract must bar using or disclosing data beyond the specified business purposes. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(1)(C) Contract must bar using data outside the direct business relationship. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(1)(D) Contract must bar merging the data with other sources, with limited exceptions and monitoring options. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ag)(2) Service providers must notify the business of subcontractors and bind them by written contract. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)(1) Defines sharing as disclosing personal information to third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)(2) Lists circumstances in which a business is not sharing personal information.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)(2)(A) Disclosure or third-party interaction intentionally directed by the consumer is not sharing. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)(2)(B) Using an identifier to signal a consumer's opt-out or limitation is not sharing. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ah)(2)(C) Transfers during mergers or acquisitions are not sharing, subject to notice duties. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ai) Defines third party by excluding certain persons, listed below.
Civ. Code §1798.140(ai)(1) The business the consumer deliberately interacts with is not a third party. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ai)(2) A service provider to the business is not a third party. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ai)(3) A contractor is not a third party. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(aj) Defines unique identifier as a persistent identifier recognizing a consumer or device over time. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.140(ak) Defines verifiable consumer request and relieves business if identity cannot be verified. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145 Exemptions
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1) Introduces activities the title does not restrict a business from doing.
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(A) Business may comply with laws, court orders or subpoenas. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(B) Business may comply with government inquiries; police may require 90-day deletion holds. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(C) Business may cooperate with law enforcement about suspected unlawful conduct. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)(i) Business may give agencies emergency access when someone faces death or serious injury.
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)(i)(I) Emergency access request requires approval by a high-ranking agency officer. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)(i)(II) Emergency request must rest on good-faith belief of lawful non-emergency access basis. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)(i)(III) Agency must seek a court order within three days or destroy the data. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(D)(ii) Seeking reproductive care services does not count as risk of death or injury. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(E) Business may exercise or defend legal claims. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(F) Business may handle deidentified or aggregate consumer information freely. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(1)(G) Conduct taking place wholly outside California is exempt from the title. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(2)
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(2)(A) The exemptions do not cover reproductive care access or search information. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(2)(B) Aggregated or deidentified data use for business purposes remains allowed if not sold or shared. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(a)(2)(C) Duty to preserve evidence in ongoing civil proceedings is unaffected. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(b) Evidentiary privilege overrides certain consumer-rights and disclosure obligations. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(c)
Civ. Code §1798.145(c)(1) Introduces categories of information the title does not apply to.

Civ. Code §1798.145(c)(1)(B) Health care providers and covered entities are exempt for patient information handled like medical data. Coming soon

Civ. Code §1798.145(g)(3)(D)(ii) Vessel equipment includes outboard engines. Coming soon

Civ. Code §1798.145(n)(2)(A) Defines independent contractor as a person serving under a written contract. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(n)(2)(B) Defines director as someone designated, elected or appointed to act as director. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.145(n)(2)(C) Defines officer as someone appointed by the board to run daily operations. Coming soon

Civ. Code §1798.150 Personal Information Security Breaches
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)(1) Consumers may sue when unencrypted personal data is stolen due to unreasonable security practices.
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)(1)(A) Remedy: statutory damages per consumer per incident, or actual damages if greater. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)(1)(B) Remedy: injunctive or declaratory relief. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)(1)(C) Remedy: any other relief the court considers appropriate. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.150(a)(2) Courts weigh seriousness, number, persistence, duration, willfulness and defendant's finances when setting damages. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.150(b) Statutory damages suits require 30 days' written notice; curing the violation can bar them. Coming soon
Civ. Code §1798.150(c) This private right of action covers only data breaches, not other CCPA violations. Coming soon
