11 CCR Art. 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS
11 CCR §7000 Title and Scope.
11 CCR §7000(a) Names the regulations and states they govern CCPA compliance without limiting other consumer rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7000(b) Violating these regulations counts as violating the CCPA. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001 Definitions.Introduces definitions used in the regulations beyond the statute's definitions.
11 CCR §7001(a) Defines the Agency as the California Privacy Protection Agency. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(b) Defines the alternative opt-out link replacing two separate opt-out links. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(c) Defines Attorney General to include Department of Justice officers and employees. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(d) Defines authorized agent as a person or entity a consumer authorises to act. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(e) Defines ADMT as technology using computation to replace or largely replace human decisions about people.
11 CCR §7001(e)(1) Substantially replacing a human means using output for decisions without qualifying human involvement.
11 CCR §7001(e)(1)(A) Human reviewer must understand how to interpret and apply the tool's result. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(e)(1)(B) Reviewer must examine the tool's result plus other relevant information before deciding. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(e)(1)(C) Reviewer must hold power to make or alter the decision after analysis. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(e)(2) Profiling counts as ADMT when it replaces or largely replaces human judgment. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(e)(3) Routine tools like hosting, caching, firewalls, spellcheckers and spreadsheets are excluded unless they replace human decisions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(f) Defines categories of sources as particular types of entities personal information comes from. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(g) Defines categories of third parties as described types of recipients of shared personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(h) Defines CCPA as the 2018 California privacy statute in the Civil Code. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(i) Defines COPPA as the federal children's online privacy law and its implementing rule. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(j) Defines cybersecurity audit as the yearly audit required for businesses posing significant security risk. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(k) Defines cybersecurity program as policies and practices protecting personal information from unauthorized access, harm, and loss of availability. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(l) Defines the cybersecurity audit report as the document produced by the audit, with contents set elsewhere. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(m) Defines disproportionate effort: response burden greatly exceeding the foreseeable benefit to the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(n) Defines employment benefits as retirement, health and similar programs accessed through an employer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(o) Defines employment-related information as personal data collected for employment purposes, a business purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(p) Defines financial incentive as any program or payment tied to collecting, keeping, selling or sharing data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(q) Defines first party as the consumer-facing business a consumer expects to deal with. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(r) Defines frictionless manner as handling opt-out preference signals per the section 7025 rules. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(s) Defines information practices as how personal data is collected, used, disclosed, sold, shared and retained. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(t) Defines information system as resources handling or giving access to personal information, owned or not. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(u) Defines multi-factor authentication as verifying at least two distinct factor types.
11 CCR §7001(u)(1) Knowledge factors, like passwords, are one authentication factor type. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(u)(2) Possession factors, like tokens, are one authentication factor type. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(u)(3) Inherence factors, like biometrics, are one authentication factor type. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(v) Defines nonbusiness as entities outside the statutory business definition, such as governments and many non-profits. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(w) Defines notice at collection as the notice given at or before data collection. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(x) Defines notice of right to limit as informing consumers they can limit sensitive data use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(y) Defines notice of right to opt out of sale or sharing of personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(z) Defines notice of financial incentive as explaining each incentive or price or service difference. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(aa) Defines opt-out preference signal as a consumer-authorised signal communicating refusal of sale and sharing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bb) Defines penetration testing as authorised attempts to defeat a system's security features. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(cc) Defines performance at work as job duties, excluding union interest, off-duty location and personal accounts. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(dd) Defines performance in an educational program as coursework, excluding personal accounts and non-coursework location. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ee) Defines physical or biological identification or profiling as automated analysis of a person's body traits. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ff) Introduces the definition of price or service difference.
11 CCR §7001(ff)(1) Price or service difference includes charging different prices tied to personal information handling. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ff)(2) Price or service difference includes differing service quality or denial tied to personal information handling. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(gg) Defines privacy policy as the statement of online and offline practices and consumer rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(hh) Defines privileged account as a user or service account with elevated abilities like managing accounts or configuration. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ii) Defines profiling as automated processing evaluating personal aspects of a person, such as behavior or location. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(jj) Defines request to access ADMT as a consumer asking for information on ADMT use about them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(kk) Defines request to appeal ADMT as a consumer appeal of ADMT use for a significant decision. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ll) Defines request to correct as asking a business to fix inaccurate personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(mm) Defines request to delete as asking a business to erase personal information collected from the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn) Defines request to know as asking a business to disclose collected personal information, in several forms.
11 CCR §7001(nn)(1) Request to know may cover the specific pieces of personal information collected. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn)(2) Request to know may cover categories of personal information collected. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn)(3) Request to know may cover categories of sources of the information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn)(4) Request to know may cover categories sold, shared or disclosed for a business purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn)(5) Request to know may cover categories of third parties receiving the information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(nn)(6) Request to know may cover the purpose for collecting, selling or sharing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(oo) Defines request to limit as asking to restrict use and disclosure of sensitive information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(pp) Defines opt-in to sale/sharing as consent by the consumer or parent for under-13s. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(qq) Defines request to opt out of ADMT as asking a business not to use ADMT on them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(rr) Defines request to opt out of sale/sharing as asking a business not to sell or share data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ss) Defines right to access ADMT as the right to get information on ADMT use about oneself. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(tt) Defines right to correct as the right to have inaccurate personal information fixed. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(uu) Defines right to delete as the right to have collected personal information erased. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(vv) Defines right to know as the right to learn what personal information was collected, sold or shared. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ww) Defines right to limit as the right to restrict use and disclosure of sensitive information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(xx) Defines right to opt out of ADMT as directing a business not to use ADMT on oneself. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(yy) Defines right to opt out of sale/sharing as directing a business to stop selling or sharing data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(zz) Defines risk assessment report as the document every required risk assessment must produce. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(aaa) Lists sensitive locations such as healthcare facilities, shelters, schools, legal offices, union offices and worship places. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb) Introduces the definition of sensitive personal information.
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1) Sensitive information includes personal information revealing certain listed categories.
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(A) Government identifiers: social security, driver's license, state ID or passport numbers are sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(B) Account or card numbers combined with access credentials are sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(C) Precise geolocation is sensitive personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(D) Racial or ethnic origin, immigration status, beliefs or union membership are sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(E) Contents of mail, email and texts are sensitive unless the business is the recipient. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(F) Genetic data is sensitive personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(1)(G) Neural data from nervous system measurement, not inferred elsewhere, is sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(2) Biometric processing used to uniquely identify a person is sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(3) Information about health, sex life or sexual orientation is sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(bbb)(4) Data of consumers known, or willfully ignored, to be under sixteen is sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ccc) Defines signed as physically signed or electronically provided under the electronic transactions law. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd) Defines significant decision as one affecting finance, housing, education, employment or healthcare access.
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(1) Financial or lending services covers credit, loans, fund transfers, accounts, check cashing and installment plans. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(2) Defines housing as places used as homes; availability or payment-only decisions are not significant. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(3) Introduces what counts as education enrollment or opportunities.
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(3)(A) Education opportunities include admission to academic or vocational programs. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(3)(B) Education opportunities include credentials like degrees, diplomas and certificates. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(3)(C) Education opportunities include suspension and expulsion. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(4) Introduces what counts as employment or contracting opportunities or compensation.
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(4)(A) Hiring counts as an employment-related significant decision. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(4)(B) Work allocation and pay, incentive or benefit decisions count as significant. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(4)(C) Promotion counts as an employment-related significant decision. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(4)(D) Demotion, suspension and termination count as employment-related significant decisions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(5) Healthcare services means diagnosis, prevention, treatment or assessment of health. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ddd)(6) Advertising to a consumer is not a significant decision. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(eee) Defines systematic observation as regular or continuous monitoring, such as tracking, recording or geofencing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(fff) Defines training of a technology as the process of it learning patterns or outputs. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(ggg) Defines third-party identity verification service as an independent provider verifying requesters, subject to Article 5. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(hhh) Defines unstructured personal information as data not retrievable in a set format without disproportionate effort. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(iii) Defines value of consumer's data as calculated under section 7081. Coming soon
11 CCR §7001(jjj) Defines verify as confirming a requester is the person whose data is held, or their guardian. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002 Restrictions on the Collection and Use of Personal Information.
11 CCR §7002(a) Collection, use, retention and sharing must be reasonably necessary and proportionate to the disclosed purposes.
11 CCR §7002(a)(1) Processing may serve the original purpose, which must match consumer expectations. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(a)(2) Processing may serve another disclosed purpose compatible with the collection context. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(b) Original purposes must fit consumers' reasonable expectations, judged by listed factors.
11 CCR §7002(b)(1) Expectations depend on the relationship between consumer and business. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(b)(2) Expectations depend on the type, nature and amount of data collected. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(b)(3) Expectations depend on the data's source and the collection method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(b)(4) Expectations depend on how clear and prominent purpose disclosures are. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(b)(5) Expectations depend on how apparent the involvement of service providers or third parties is. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(c) Compatibility of another purpose is judged by three listed considerations.
11 CCR §7002(c)(1) Consider consumers' reasonable expectations at collection time, using the earlier factors. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(c)(2) Consider the further purpose, including whether it is a listed business purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(c)(3) Consider how strongly the original expectations link to the further purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(d) Data handling must be necessary and proportionate to each purpose or consented purpose.
11 CCR §7002(d)(1) Collect only the minimum personal information needed for the purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(d)(2) Weigh possible negative impacts on consumers from collecting or processing the data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(d)(3) Consider safeguards, such as encryption or timed deletion, addressing identified negative impacts. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(e) Obtain consent before processing for purposes outside the permitted ones; consent must be withdrawable. Coming soon
11 CCR §7002(f) Do not collect categories beyond those in the notice; give new notice for additions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003 Requirements for Disclosures and Communications to Consumers.
11 CCR §7003(a) Consumer disclosures must be readable and understandable, in plain language without jargon. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003(b) Article 2 disclosures must also meet further listed requirements.
11 CCR §7003(b)(1) Disclosures must be legible, including on small screens. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003(b)(2) Disclosures must be offered in languages the business normally uses with California consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003(b)(3) Disclosures must be accessible to disabled people; online ones follow WCAG 2.1, others give alternatives. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003(c) Website links required by the law must look as prominent as neighbouring links. Coming soon
11 CCR §7003(d) Mobile apps must reach the privacy policy from the store page and inside the app. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004 Requirements for Methods for Submitting CCPA Requests and Obtaining Consumer Consent.
11 CCR §7004(a) Request and consent methods must follow the listed design principles.
11 CCR §7004(a)(1) Request and consent methods must use plain, readable language and meet section 7003. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(2) Choosing the privacy-protective option must not take more effort than the alternative.
11 CCR §7004(a)(2)(A) Opting out of sale or sharing must not need more steps than opting in. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(2)(B) Opt-in prompts offering only yes or later, with no decline, are asymmetric. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(2)(C) Consent banners offering accept-all but only a preferences route are asymmetric. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(2)(D) A more eye-catching yes button than the no button is asymmetric. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(2)(E) Financial incentive participation must not be preselected or visually favoured over declining. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(3) Consent interfaces must avoid confusing wording, double negatives, deception; silence is not consent.
11 CCR §7004(a)(3)(A) Yes/No choices beside a negatively worded do-not-sell statement are confusing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(3)(B) Bare on/off toggles without explanatory wording are confusing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(3)(C) Switching the usual order of confirm buttons against expectations is confusing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(3)(D) Dismissing a consent pop-up without explicitly accepting must not count as consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(3)(E) Fake urgency, such as bogus countdowns beside consent choices, is misleading. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(4) Choice architecture must not impair free, specific, informed, unambiguous consent.
11 CCR §7004(a)(4)(A) Opt-out requests must not require clicking through disruptive screens. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(4)(B) Consent for incompatible uses must be separate from consent for necessary uses. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(4)(C) Consent cannot be gained by accepting broad terms mixing in unrelated content. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(5) Submitting requests or giving or withdrawing consent must be low-friction and tested to work.
11 CCR §7004(a)(5)(A) The opt-out link must lead straight to the mechanism, not require searching a policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(5)(B) Known broken or circular links and unmonitored request inboxes may violate the rule. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(5)(C) Unnecessary waiting, duplicate forms or delays between submissions may violate the rule. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(a)(5)(D) Staff on toll-free request lines must be able to process CCPA requests. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(b) Non-compliant methods may be dark patterns, and consent obtained through them is void. Coming soon
11 CCR §7004(c) An interface is a dark pattern if it subverts choice, regardless of intent. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 2 REQUIRED DISCLOSURES TO CONSUMERS
11 CCR §7010 Overview of Required Disclosures.
11 CCR §7010(a) Every covered business must publish a privacy policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(b) Businesses controlling collection from consumers must give a Notice at Collection. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(c) Businesses using automated decision technology must provide a Pre-use Notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(d) The Pre-use Notice must link to an opt-out of automated decision technology, with exceptions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(e) Businesses selling or sharing personal information must give an opt-out notice or alternative link. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(f) Businesses using sensitive data beyond permitted purposes must give a Notice of Right to Limit. Coming soon
11 CCR §7010(g) Businesses offering financial incentives or price differences must give a notice about them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011 Privacy Policy.
11 CCR §7011(a) The privacy policy must describe information practices and explain consumer rights and how to use them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(b) The privacy policy must meet the readability and language requirements of section 7003. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(c) The privacy policy must be printable as a document. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(d) Policy must be posted online behind a conspicuous privacy link, including in app settings. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e) The privacy policy must contain the following listed information.
11 CCR §7011(e)(1) Policy must comprehensively describe online and offline information practices.
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(A) List personal information categories collected in the past twelve months, using statutory terms. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(B) List the categories of sources personal information comes from. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(C) State the business or commercial purposes for collecting personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(D) Identify categories sold or shared in the past year, or say none were. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(E) For each sold or shared category, name the categories of recipient third parties. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(F) State the purposes for selling or sharing personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(G) Say whether the business knowingly sells or shares data of under-16s. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(H) Identify categories disclosed to service providers or contractors, or state none were. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(I) State the purposes for disclosing personal information to service providers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(1)(J) Say whether sensitive data is used or disclosed beyond permitted purposes. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2) Policy must explain consumers' CCPA rights regarding their personal information.
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(A) Explain the right to know what data was collected, sources, purposes, recipients. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(B) Explain the right to delete collected personal information, subject to exceptions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(C) Explain the right to correct inaccurate personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(D) Where data is sold or shared, explain the right to opt out. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(E) Where sensitive data is used beyond permitted purposes, explain the right to limit. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(F) Where automated decision technology is used, explain the right to opt out of it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(G) Where automated decision technology is used, explain the right to access information about it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(2)(H) Explain the right against retaliation, including for applicants, students, employees and contractors. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3) Policy must explain how to exercise rights and what to expect.
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(A) Explain the methods consumers can use to exercise their rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(B) Give request instructions, including links to any online form or portal. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(C) Include the opt-out-of-sale notice contents or a link to it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(D) Include the Right to Limit notice contents or a link to it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(E) Describe how requests are verified and what information the consumer must supply. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(F) Explain how opt-out preference signals are processed and how consumers can use them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(G) If signals are honoured frictionlessly, explain how consumers can enable that. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(H) Give instructions for authorized agents making requests for a consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(I) If selling under-16 data knowingly, describe the consent processes in sections 7070 and 7071. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(3)(J) Privacy policy must list a contact for privacy questions, matching how the business mainly deals with consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(4) State when the privacy policy was last updated. Coming soon
11 CCR §7011(e)(5) Include or link the metrics reporting required by section 7102, where applicable. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012 Notice at Collection of Personal Information.
11 CCR §7012(a) Notice at Collection gives timely information on categories, purposes and sale or sharing before collection. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(b) The Notice at Collection must meet section 7003 readability and language requirements. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(c) Notice must be readily available wherever consumers encounter collection, at or before it.
11 CCR §7012(c)(1) Online collection: link the notice on the introductory page and collecting pages. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(c)(2) Web forms: place the notice link near the input fields or submit button. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(c)(3) Mobile apps: link the notice on the download page and within the app. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(c)(4) Offline collection: use printed forms, paper copies, or signage pointing to the notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(c)(5) Phone or in-person collection: the notice may be given orally. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(d) Without giving the notice at or before collection, personal information must not be collected. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e) The Notice at Collection must contain the following listed items.
11 CCR §7012(e)(1) List categories of personal information to be collected, including sensitive ones, in meaningful terms. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e)(2) State the purposes for which each category is collected and used. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e)(3) Say whether each category is sold or shared. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e)(4) State retention period per category, or the criteria determining it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e)(5) When selling or sharing, include the opt-out notice link or its online location. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(e)(6) Include a link to the privacy policy or say where it is online. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(f) Online notice may link directly to the policy section containing the required details. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(g) Third-party controllers of collection have duties; first party's opt-out obligations remain unchanged.
11 CCR §7012(g)(1) Both first party and third party controlling collection must give notice, possibly jointly. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(g)(2) A third party collecting on another's premises must display notice conspicuously there. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(g)(3) Examples follow illustrating notice duties.
11 CCR §7012(g)(3)(A) Example: website owner links its notice; ad network gives its own or is included. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(g)(3)(B) Example: coffee shop signage plus Wi-Fi provider's notice before connection. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(g)(3)(C) Example: car rental gives notice at counter; vehicle data collector signs in car. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(h) Businesses neither collecting directly nor selling or sharing need no Notice at Collection. Coming soon
11 CCR §7012(i) Registered data brokers collecting indirectly are exempt if registration links an opt-out policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013 Notice of Right to Opt-out of Sale/Sharing and the “Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information” Link.
11 CCR §7013(a) The opt-out notice and link let consumers stop sale or sharing, immediately or via a page. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(b) The opt-out notice must meet section 7003 readability and language requirements. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(c) The Do Not Sell or Share link must be conspicuous, in homepage header or footer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(d) An alternative link or frictionless signal processing may replace the link, but the notice remains. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e) Sellers or sharers must deliver the opt-out notice as follows.
11 CCR §7013(e)(1) Post the opt-out notice on the page the link opens, or link to the policy section. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(2) Businesses without a website must document and follow another compliant notification method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(3) Give the opt-out notice in the same manner the data is collected.
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(A) Offline collection requires offline notice, such as paper forms or signage. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(B) Data collected by phone requires oral notice during the call. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(C) Connected devices must show the notice before or when collection starts. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(D) Augmented or virtual reality collection requires notice at one of two points.
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(D)(1) Notice before or when the consumer enters the AR or VR environment. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(e)(3)(D)(2) Notice before or when the consumer meets the business inside the environment. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(f) The opt-out notice must contain the following listed content.
11 CCR §7013(f)(1) Opt-out notice must explain the consumer's right to stop sale or sharing of data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(f)(2) Notice must explain how to submit an opt-out, including an online form or offline method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(g) Introduces conditions under which the opt-out notice and link can be omitted.
11 CCR §7013(g)(1) Exemption applies only if the business neither sells nor shares personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(g)(2) Exemption also requires the privacy policy to say no selling or sharing occurs. Coming soon
11 CCR §7013(h) Data collected while no opt-out notice was posted can't be sold or shared without consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014 Notice of Right to Limit and the “Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information” Link.
11 CCR §7014(a) Describes the purpose of the limit notice and link: let consumers restrict sensitive data use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(b) The limit notice must meet the general clarity and readability standards of section 7003. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(c) Limit link must be conspicuous and placed in the homepage header or footer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(d) Business may use the alternative opt-out link instead, but still posts the limit notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e) Businesses using sensitive data beyond permitted purposes must give the limit notice as described.
11 CCR §7014(e)(1) Post the limit notice on the page the link leads to, or link to policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(2) Businesses without websites must set up and follow another documented way to inform consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(3) Limit notice must be delivered through the same channel where sensitive data is collected.
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(A) For in-person collection, give the limit notice offline, such as on forms or signage. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(B) For phone collection, give the limit notice verbally during the call. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(C) For connected devices, show the limit notice before or when collection starts. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(D) For augmented or virtual reality collection, notice must reach consumers at specified moments.
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(D)(1) One option: show the limit notice before the user enters the AR/VR environment. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(e)(3)(D)(2) Other option: show the limit notice before or when data is gathered in AR/VR. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(f) Lists what the limit notice must contain.
11 CCR §7014(f)(1) Limit notice must describe the consumer's right to limit sensitive data use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(f)(2) Limit notice must give submission instructions, including an online form or offline method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(g) Introduces conditions under which the limit notice and link can be omitted.
11 CCR §7014(g)(1) Exempt if sensitive data is used only for permitted purposes and the policy says so. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(g)(2) Exempt if sensitive data isn't used to infer traits and the policy says so. Coming soon
11 CCR §7014(h) Sensitive data collected without a posted limit notice can't be used beyond permitted purposes absent consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015 Alternative Opt- out Link.
11 CCR §7015(a) Alternative single link lets consumers exercise both opt-out and limit rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015(b) Alternative link must carry a prescribed title and the opt-out icon beside it.
11 CCR §7015(b)(1) Alternative link must be conspicuous and sit in the homepage header or footer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015(b)(2) Icon size should roughly match other icons in the header or footer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015(b)(3) Icon colours may be adjusted so it stays visible against the background. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015(c) Alternative link's destination page must contain specified information.
11 CCR §7015(c)(1) Destination page must describe both the opt-out and limit rights clearly. Coming soon
11 CCR §7015(c)(2) Page needs an easy, minimal-step online mechanism to exercise both rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016 Notice of Financial Incentive.
11 CCR §7016(a) Financial incentive notice explains material terms; not needed if no incentive is offered. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(b) Incentive notice must meet the section 7003 clarity and readability standards. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(c) Incentive notice must be readily available before the consumer opts in. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d) Lists the contents required in the financial incentive notice.
11 CCR §7016(d)(1) Incentive notice includes a brief summary of the offer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d)(2) Describe material terms, affected data categories, and the value of the consumer's data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d)(3) Explain how a consumer can opt in to the incentive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d)(4) State the right to withdraw anytime and how to do so. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d)(5) Explain how any price or service difference relates reasonably to data value.
11 CCR §7016(d)(5)(A) Provide a good-faith estimate of the data's value underlying the difference. Coming soon
11 CCR §7016(d)(5)(B) Describe the methods used to compute the data's value. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 3 BUSINESS PRACTICES FOR HANDLING CONSUMER REQUESTS
11 CCR §7020 Methods for Submitting Requests to Delete, Requests to Correct , and Requests to Know.
11 CCR §7020(a) Online-only businesses with direct consumer relationships need just an email address for requests. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(b) Other businesses need two or more request methods, including a toll-free number and website form. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(c) Choose request methods based on how the business mainly deals with consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(d) Online deletion requests may require a second confirmation step, if otherwise compliant. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(e) Where data is kept over a year, requests to know must cover older data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(f) Requests sent by non-designated or flawed means must be handled in one of two ways.
11 CCR §7020(f)(1) One option: process the misdirected request as though properly submitted. Coming soon
11 CCR §7020(f)(2) Other option: tell the consumer how to submit correctly or fix deficiencies. Coming soon
11 CCR §7021 Timelines for Responding to Requests to Delete, Requests to Correct, Requests to Know, Requests to Access ADMT, and Requests to Appeal ADMT.
11 CCR §7021(a) Confirm receipt of privacy requests within ten business days, explaining verification and timing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7021(b) Respond within 45 days, extendable to 90 with notice and explanation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022 Requests to Delete.
11 CCR §7022(a) Deletion may be denied if identity can't be verified; tell the requestor. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(b) Lists the steps a business must take to comply with deletion requests.
11 CCR §7022(b)(1) Erase, deidentify or aggregate the data in live systems, excluding backups. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(b)(2) Tell service providers and contractors to delete the data they hold under contract. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(b)(3) Notify third parties who received the data, unless impossible, and explain any such claim. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(c) Service providers must cooperate with deletion requests when notified by the business.
11 CCR §7022(c)(1) Providers erase, deidentify, aggregate data, or enable the business to do so. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(c)(2) Where an exception applies, delete the rest and use retained data only for that exception. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(c)(3) Providers must pass deletion notices on to their own subcontractors. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(c)(4) Providers notify others who accessed data through them, absent impossibility or disproportionate effort. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(d) Deletion from archived or backup systems may wait until they are restored or accessed. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(e) Tell the consumer whether deletion was done and that a record of the request is kept. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(f) Lists duties when a deletion request is denied in whole or part.
11 CCR §7022(f)(1) Give a detailed explanation of the grounds for denying deletion. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(f)(2) Still delete information that isn't covered by the exception. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(f)(3) Use retained data solely for the exception's purpose. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(f)(4) Instruct service providers and contractors to delete non-excepted data and limit retained data use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(g) After denying deletion, offer opt-out of sale or sharing if the consumer hasn't already. Coming soon
11 CCR §7022(h) Selective deletion choices are allowed only alongside a delete-everything option; disclose other deletion abilities. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023 Requests to Correct .
11 CCR §7023(a) Correction may be denied if identity can't be verified; tell the requestor. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(b) Judge accuracy on all circumstances; deny if data is more likely accurate.
11 CCR §7023(b)(1) Circumstances to weigh when judging accuracy include several listed factors.
11 CCR §7023(b)(1)(A) Consider what kind of information it is, such as objective or sensitive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(b)(1)(B) Consider how the business obtained the disputed information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(b)(1)(C) Consider documentation about accuracy from any source. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(b)(2) If business isn't the source and lacks documentation, consumer's claim can suffice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(c) Apply corrections in systems, keep them corrected, and instruct service providers to correct too.
11 CCR §7023(c)(1) Example: corrected data must not be overwritten by later inaccurate data broker feeds. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(c)(2) Example: backup copies may be corrected later when restored or next used. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d) Heading for documentation rules in correction requests.
11 CCR §7023(d)(1) Accept and consider any documentation the consumer supplies for a correction. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(2) Business may demand documentation only as needed to rebut its own evidence, weighing factors.
11 CCR §7023(d)(2)(A) Weigh the nature of the information when deciding on documentation needs. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(2)(B) Weigh how trustworthy and verifiable the business's supporting documentation is. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(2)(C) Weigh the purpose of using the information; essential data may justify more proof. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(2)(D) Weigh impact on the consumer; harmful data warrants less documentation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(3) Correction documentation may only be used for correcting and recordkeeping. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(d)(4) Keep correction-request documentation under reasonable security procedures. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(e) Deletion may replace correction only if it doesn't harm the consumer or they consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(f) Tell the consumer whether correction was done, with duties on denial.
11 CCR §7023(f)(1) Explain the grounds for denying a correction. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(f)(2) Impossibility claims need a detailed, fact-based explanation, not a bare assertion. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(f)(3) For denied health-data corrections, tell consumer about a 250-word statement option. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(f)(4) If data is deletable, tell the consumer they can request deletion and how. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(g) Repeat correction request denied within six months may be refused unless new documentation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(h) Deny correction believed fraudulent or abusive, with documented belief and explanation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(i) If another party was the source, name it or tell it to correct. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(j) Let consumers confirm corrections; withhold highly sensitive identifiers but offer matching confirmation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7023(k) Measures keeping corrected data from being overwritten count toward correction compliance. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024 Requests to Know.
11 CCR §7024(a) Without verification, never disclose specific personal information; evaluate as a category request. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(b) Unverified category requests may be denied; point consumer to privacy policy practices. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(c) Search isn't required for data meeting all listed conditions.
11 CCR §7024(c)(1) Condition: the data isn't held in a searchable or accessible format. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(c)(2) Condition: data is kept only for legal or compliance reasons. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(c)(3) Condition for withholding search: business neither sells the data nor uses it commercially. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(c)(4) Business must tell the consumer which record categories went unsearched under the exemption. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(d) Never disclose sensitive identifiers like SSNs, account numbers, passwords or biometric data in know responses.
11 CCR §7024(d)(1) Tell the consumer the type of sensitive data held, without revealing the data itself. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(d)(2) Offer a way for verified consumers to confirm held data matches what they supply. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(e) When denying a verified request for specific information, the business must follow listed steps.
11 CCR §7024(e)(1) Give a detailed explanation of the denial basis, including legal conflicts or exceptions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(e)(2) Still disclose the portion of personal information not covered by the exception. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(f) Use reasonable security when sending personal information to the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(g) Password-protected account holders may be served through a secure, verified self-service portal with full disclosure. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(h) Provide all personal information from the prior twelve months, and older data since 2022 unless disproportionate. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(i) Service providers and contractors must help the business answer requests to know. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(j) Category-based know responses must be individualized, not just pointing to the privacy policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k) Responses to category requests must include a set of specified items.
11 CCR §7024(k)(1) List the categories of personal information collected about the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k)(2) List the categories of sources the information came from. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k)(3) State the business or commercial purpose for collecting, selling or sharing the data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k)(4) List categories of third parties receiving the personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k)(5) Identify categories sold or shared, with third-party categories per information category. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(k)(6) Identify categories disclosed for a business purpose, with recipient service provider categories for each. Coming soon
11 CCR §7024(l) Describe categories clearly enough that consumers meaningfully understand them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025 Opt-out Preference Signals.
11 CCR §7025(a) Explains that opt-out preference signals let consumers opt out of sale/sharing automatically everywhere. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(b) Businesses selling or sharing data must treat qualifying opt-out signals as valid opt-out requests.
11 CCR §7025(b)(1) A valid signal must use a commonly recognized format, such as an HTTP header. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(b)(2) The signal sender must make clear that using it means opting out of sale/sharing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c) Sets duties when an online business detects a compliant opt-out preference signal.
11 CCR §7025(c)(1) Treat the signal as an opt-out for the browser, device, profiles and known consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(2) Don't demand extra information to honor the signal; any voluntary data is used only for that. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(3) Signal overrides a conflicting setting, though the business may ask the consumer to consent again. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(4) Where the signal conflicts with a financial incentive program, business may ask the consumer to confirm withdrawal. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(5) Absence of a signal after a prior one must not be read as opt-in. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(6) Website must display whether the opt-out signal was processed as a valid request. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(7) Introduces illustrative examples of opt-out signal handling.
11 CCR §7025(c)(7)(A) Example: anonymous browser signal stops browser-linked sharing but cannot reach unlinked account data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(7)(B) Example: logged-in user's signal overrides default settings and applies to account and offline sales. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(7)(C) Example: signal applies to account; a later device without signal isn't consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(7)(D) Example: incentive program member's signal may be ignored after conflict notice and non-withdrawal. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(c)(7)(E) Example: after clearing cookies, the signal must be honored for the unrecognized browser. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(d) Information gathered for sending or processing opt-out signals may not be used for other purposes. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(e) Statute gives businesses a choice regarding signals and opt-out links.
11 CCR §7025(e)(1) Option one: process signals and also post the opt-out and limit links. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(e)(2) Option two: process signals frictionlessly and skip links; signals must be honored regardless. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(f) Defines what frictionless signal processing means: listed things the business must not do.
11 CCR §7025(f)(1) No fee or valuable consideration may be required of consumers using a signal. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(f)(2) Consumers using a signal must get the same product experience as others. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(f)(3) No pop-ups or interstitial content in response to the signal, except status display. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g) Businesses may skip the opt-out link if they meet additional requirements.
11 CCR §7025(g)(1) Process the opt-out signal frictionlessly. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(2) Privacy policy must contain specified opt-out information.
11 CCR §7025(g)(2)(A) Privacy policy describes the right to opt out of sale or sharing. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(2)(B) Privacy policy states that signals are processed frictionlessly. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(2)(C) Privacy policy explains how consumers can enable signals. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(2)(D) Privacy policy gives instructions for any other opt-out methods. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(3) Signal must fully effectuate the opt-out without requiring extra information, including offline sales.
11 CCR §7025(g)(3)(A) Example: offline selling needing login means the link exemption is unavailable. Coming soon
11 CCR §7025(g)(3)(B) Example: online-only seller may use the exemption and omit the opt-out link. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026 Requests to Opt-out of Sale/Sharing.
11 CCR §7026(a) Sellers or sharers must offer two or more opt-out methods, one matching main interaction.
11 CCR §7026(a)(1) Online collectors must accept opt-out signals plus a form or link method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(a)(2) Businesses dealing in person and online may add an in-person opt-out method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(a)(3) Other acceptable opt-out methods include phone, email, in-person form and mail. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(a)(4) A cookie banner alone is not an acceptable opt-out method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(b) Opt-out methods must be easy, minimal-step and follow the design rules of section 7004. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(c) Opt-out can't require account creation or unnecessary additional information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(d) Opt-out requests need no verification; do it without extra data when possible. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(e) A documented good-faith belief of fraud allows denial with an explanation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(f) Describes how a business must carry out an opt-out request.
11 CCR §7026(f)(1) Stop selling or sharing as soon as feasible, within fifteen business days. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(f)(2) Tell third parties who received the data to comply and pass the request on. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(f)(3) Introduces illustrative examples of carrying out opt-out requests.
11 CCR §7026(f)(3)(A) Example: real-time bidding sellers able to stop instantly must comply immediately. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(f)(3)(B) Example: batch seller must notify clients who got data before the request took effect. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(g) Provide a way for consumers to confirm their opt-out was processed. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(h) Granular opt-out choices allowed only with a single opt-out-of-all option; affects signal exemption. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(i) Telling a consumer of a charge after opt-out requires a financial incentive notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(j) Authorized agents may submit opt-outs with signed permission, except for signals. Coming soon
11 CCR §7026(k) Wait at least twelve months before asking an opted-out consumer to consent again. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027 Requests to Limit Use and Disclosure of Sensitive Personal Information.
11 CCR §7027(a) Explains the purpose of the right to limit sensitive personal information use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(b) Businesses using sensitive data beyond permitted purposes need two or more limit-request methods.
11 CCR §7027(b)(1) Online collectors must offer an interactive form via the limit link or alternative link. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(b)(2) Businesses dealing in person and online may add an in-person limit method. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(b)(3) Other acceptable limit methods include phone, email, in-person form and mail. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(b)(4) A cookie banner alone does not qualify as a method to limit. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(c) Limit methods must be easy, minimal-step and follow section 7004 design rules. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(d) Limit requests can't require an account or unnecessary extra information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(e) Limit requests need no verification; comply without extra data when possible. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(f) A documented good-faith belief of fraud allows denying a limit request with explanation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(g) Describes how a business must comply with a request to limit.
11 CCR §7027(g)(1) Stop non-permitted use and disclosure of sensitive data within fifteen business days. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(g)(2) Notify service providers and contractors to comply with the limit within the same period. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(g)(3) Notify third parties holding the sensitive data to comply and forward the request. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(h) Provide a way for consumers to confirm their limit request was processed. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(i) May offer choices to allow specific uses if a single limit-all option exists. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(j) Authorized agents may submit limit requests with the consumer's signed written permission. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(k) Telling a consumer of a charge after a limit request requires a financial incentive notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(l) Wait twelve months before asking a consumer who limited use to consent again. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m) Lists purposes for which sensitive data may be used without offering a right to limit.
11 CCR §7027(m)(1) Sensitive data may be used to deliver goods or services an average consumer expects. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(2) Sensitive data may be used to prevent, detect and investigate incidents harming data security.
11 CCR §7027(m)(2)(A) Example: sharing login details with a hired security firm investigating a breach. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(2)(B) Example: scanning staff outgoing email to stop leaks, but not for other aims. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(3) Sensitive data may be used to resist malicious, deceptive, fraudulent or illegal actions.
11 CCR §7027(m)(3)(A) Example: using ethnicity or message contents to investigate discrimination or hate speech claims. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(3)(B) Example: employee biometrics for secure-area access, with no indefinite retention or unrelated use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(4) Sensitive data may be used to protect people's physical safety. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(5) Sensitive data may be used briefly for transient, non-profiling, non-disclosed purposes like contextual ads. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(6) Sensitive data may be used for services performed on the business's behalf. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(7) Sensitive data may be used to verify quality or safety and improve own products. Coming soon
11 CCR §7027(m)(8) Sensitive data may be processed when not intended to infer characteristics about the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7028 Requests to Opt-in After Opting-out of the Sale or Sharing of Personal Information or Limiting the Use and Disclosure of Sensitive Personal Information.
11 CCR §7028(a) Opt-in after opting out needs a request followed by a separate confirmation. Coming soon
11 CCR §7028(b) Business may tell opted-out consumers a service needs sale or sharing, and explain how to consent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7028(c) Business may explain that a service needs extra sensitive data uses and how to consent. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 4 SERVICE PROVIDERS, CONTRACTORS, AND THIRD PARTIES
11 CCR §7050 Service Providers and Contractors.
11 CCR §7050(a) Service providers may retain, use or disclose data only for limited, necessary, proportionate purposes.
11 CCR §7050(a)(1) Permitted use: the specific business purposes named in the written contract. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(a)(2) Permitted use: engaging a qualifying subcontractor as another service provider. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(a)(3) Permitted use: internal improvement of its services, not for serving other parties.
11 CCR §7050(a)(3)(A) Example: email provider may analyse engagement to improve services but not mail for others. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(a)(3)(B) Example: shipper may fix faulty addresses but not compile them for ads or sale. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(a)(4) Permitted use: detecting security incidents and fraud, even if the contract omits it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(a)(5) Permitted use: purposes listed in the Civil Code's statutory exemptions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(b) Service providers cannot provide cross-context behavioral advertising or combine opted-out consumers' data.
11 CCR §7050(b)(1) Example: social platform may serve demographic ads but not match customer email lists. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(b)(2) Example: an ad agency may place contextual ads on relevant websites. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(c) Service providers receiving consumer requests must follow business instructions or tell the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(d) A provider that is itself a business must comply for data outside its provider role. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(e) Without a compliant contract, a recipient is not a service provider; disclosure may be a sale. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(f) Service providers must comply with the terms of their required contract. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(g) Whether a nonbusiness's service provider must honour requests depends on its own business status. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(h) Service providers must cooperate with the business on audits and risk assessments.
11 CCR §7050(h)(1) Provide the auditor relevant information for the cybersecurity audit without misrepresenting facts. Coming soon
11 CCR §7050(h)(2) Supply facts needed for risk assessments without misrepresenting them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051 Contract Requirements for Service Providers and Contractors.
11 CCR §7051(a) Sets the required content of service provider and contractor contracts.
11 CCR §7051(a)(1) Contract must forbid the provider selling or sharing the personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(2) Contract must name specific business purposes, not generic references, for the disclosure. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(3) Contract must bar retaining, using or disclosing data beyond the specified purposes. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(4) Contract must bar use outside the direct relationship, such as combining with other data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(5) Contract must require CCPA compliance, equal privacy protection and reasonable security practices. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(6) Contract must let the business take steps like audits to verify proper use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(7) Contract must require notice when the provider can no longer meet obligations. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(8) Contract must let the business stop and remediate unauthorised use after notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(a)(9) Contract must ensure the provider helps fulfil consumer requests or receives them from the business. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(b) Providers using subcontractors must have CCPA-compliant contracts with them. Coming soon
11 CCR §7051(c) Due diligence on providers affects whether a business can claim no reason to suspect violations. Coming soon
11 CCR §7052 Third Parties.
11 CCR §7052(a) Third parties without a compliant contract may not handle the personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7052(b) Third parties must follow their contract and treat data as the business must. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053 Contract Requirements for Third Parties.
11 CCR §7053(a) Businesses selling or sharing data with third parties need a written agreement with set terms.
11 CCR §7053(a)(1) Agreement must identify specific, limited purposes for making the data available. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(a)(2) Agreement must restrict the third party's use to the specified purposes. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(a)(3) Agreement must require CCPA compliance, equal protection and reasonable security by the third party. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(a)(4) Agreement must let the business take steps to verify consistent use. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(a)(5) Agreement must let the business stop and remediate unauthorised use after notice. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(a)(6) Agreement must require notice if the third party can no longer comply. Coming soon
11 CCR §7053(b) Due diligence on third parties affects the business's defence of not knowing about violations. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 5 VERIFICATION OF REQUESTS
11 CCR §7060 General Rules Regarding Verification .
11 CCR §7060(a) Business must have a documented, reasonable method to verify requesters are the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(b) No identity verification for opt-out or limit requests; asks must not be burdensome. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c) Sets how a business must choose its verification method.
11 CCR §7060(c)(1) Match supplied identifiers to data already held before asking for more. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(2) Avoid collecting sensitive statutory data types unless needed for verification. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3) Weigh listed risk factors when choosing the verification method.
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(A) More sensitive and valuable data requires stricter verification. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(B) Greater harm from unauthorised deletion, correction or access requires stricter verification. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(C) Higher likelihood of attackers targeting the data requires stricter verification. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(D) Consider whether verification data is robust against spoofing or fabrication. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(E) Consider how the business interacts with the consumer. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(c)(3)(F) Consider what verification technology is available. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(d) Avoid asking for extra verification data; delete it promptly after processing the request. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(e) Business may not charge a fee for verifying delete, correct or know requests. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(f) Business must use reasonable security to detect fraudulent verification and prevent unauthorised changes or access. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(g) Deidentified data need not be provided, deleted or re-identified for requests. Coming soon
11 CCR §7060(h) Correction requests must be verified using information other than the disputed data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7061 Verification for Password -Protected Accounts.
11 CCR §7061(a) Password-protected accounts may use existing authentication; reauthenticate before deletion, correction or disclosure. Coming soon
11 CCR §7061(b) If account fraud is suspected, withhold action until further verification succeeds. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062 Verification for Non-Accountholders.
11 CCR §7062(a) Non-accountholder requests must meet this section plus the general verification rules. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(b) Requests to know categories need reasonable certainty, such as matching two data points. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(c) Requests for specific pieces need high certainty, such as three data points and a signed declaration. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(d) Delete and correct requests need certainty scaled to data sensitivity and harm risk. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(e) Introduces illustrative examples of non-accountholder verification.
11 CCR §7062(e)(1) Example: verify via details of recent purchases when records tie to a named person. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(e)(2) Example: for unnamed app data, have the consumer prove sole association with it. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(f) Deny requests for specific pieces or ADMT access when the requestor cannot be verified. Coming soon
11 CCR §7062(g) If verification is impossible, say so and explain, and reassess annually. Coming soon
11 CCR §7063 Authorized Agents.
11 CCR §7063(a) Business may require proof of signed permission when an authorized agent submits a request.
11 CCR §7063(a)(1) Business may require the consumer to verify their own identity directly. Coming soon
11 CCR §7063(a)(2) Business may require the consumer to confirm they authorised the agent, without resubmitting. Coming soon
11 CCR §7063(b) Power of attorney exempts from proof rules and cannot be demanded for agents. Coming soon
11 CCR §7063(c) Authorized agents must keep reasonable security protecting the consumer's information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7063(d) Agents may use consumer data only for the request, verification or fraud prevention. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 6 SPECIAL RULES REGARDING CONSUMERS LESS THAN 16 YEARS OF AGE
11 CCR §7070 Consumers Less Than 13 Years of Age .
11 CCR §7070(a) Heading for the process of opting in to sale or sharing for children.
11 CCR §7070(a)(1) Business knowingly selling children's data under 13 must verify the consenting person is the parent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2) Lists methods reasonably ensuring the consenting person is the child's parent or guardian.
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(A) Method: signed consent form under penalty of perjury returned by mail, fax or scan. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(B) Method: parent uses a card or payment system notifying the account holder of transactions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(C) Method: parent calls a toll-free line staffed by trained personnel. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(D) Method: parent connects with trained personnel by videoconference. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(E) Method: parent communicates in person with trained personnel. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(a)(2)(F) Method: check government ID against databases, then promptly delete the ID. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(b) After parental consent to sale, tell the parent about opting out and how. Coming soon
11 CCR §7070(c) Document and follow a reasonable way to confirm a requester is a child's parent. Coming soon
11 CCR §7071 Consumers at Least 13 Years of Age and Less Than 16 Years of Age.
11 CCR §7071(a) Businesses knowingly selling data of 13-15 year olds need a documented opt-in process. Coming soon
11 CCR §7071(b) When a teen opts in, explain their continuing right to opt out later. Coming soon
11 CCR §7072 Notices to Consumers Less Than 16 Years of Age.
11 CCR §7072(a) Privacy policy must describe the processes for minors' consent and opt-in. Coming soon
11 CCR §7072(b) Businesses aimed only at under-16s, selling only with consent, may skip the opt-out notice. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 7 NON-DISCRIMINATION
11 CCR §7080 Discriminatory Practices.
11 CCR §7080(a) Charging or serving consumers differently for exercising privacy rights is prohibited discrimination. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(b) Price or service differences are allowed only if reasonably tied to data value. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(c) Lawfully denying a privacy request is not itself discriminatory. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(d) Introduces illustrative examples of discriminatory practices.
11 CCR §7080(d)(1) Example: letting only paying subscribers opt out of sale is discriminatory absent data-value justification. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(d)(2) Example: a loyalty member's deletion request may be partly denied where data is needed for the program. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(d)(3) Example: removing loyalty access after an opt-out is discriminatory unless justified by data value. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(d)(4) Example: stopping coupons after deletion is discriminatory unless value-related; email deletion cannot be refused. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(e) Notify consumers of any financial incentive or price difference, per section 7016. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(f) A permitted reasonable fee for requests is not a regulated financial incentive. Coming soon
11 CCR §7080(g) Price or service differences required by state or federal law are not discriminatory. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081 Calculating the Value of Consumer Data.
11 CCR §7081(a) Use and document a good-faith method to value consumer data for any price difference.
11 CCR §7081(a)(1) Valuation factor: marginal value of selling, collecting or deleting one consumer's data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(2) Valuation factor: average value of selling, collecting or deleting consumer data. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(3) Valuation factor: total data value divided by number of consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(4) Valuation factor: revenue from selling, collecting or retaining personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(5) Valuation factor: costs of selling, collecting or retaining personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(6) Valuation factor: costs of providing the incentive or price difference. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(7) Valuation factor: profit from selling, collecting or retaining personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(a)(8) Valuation factor: any other reliable method applied in good faith. Coming soon
11 CCR §7081(b) Data value may be measured across all people in the United States, not just consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 8 TRAINING AND RECORD-KEEPING
11 CCR §7100 Training.
11 CCR §7100(a) Staff handling privacy inquiries must know CCPA requirements and how consumers exercise rights. Coming soon
11 CCR §7100(b) Businesses handling data of 10 million or more consumers need a documented training policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7101 Record-Keeping.
11 CCR §7101(a) Keep consumer request records 24 months, securely protected. Coming soon
11 CCR §7101(b) Request logs must capture dates, request type, channel, response and denial basis. Coming soon
11 CCR §7101(c) Keeping required request records, if unused otherwise, does not alone violate the CCPA. Coming soon
11 CCR §7101(d) Request records may only serve compliance review and not be shared with third parties. Coming soon
11 CCR §7101(e) No duty to retain personal information solely to fulfil requests, beyond required records. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102 Requirements for Businesses Collecting Large Amounts of Personal Information.
11 CCR §7102(a) Large-volume businesses (10 million consumers) have extra metrics duties listed below.
11 CCR §7102(a)(1) Compile prior-year request metrics.
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(A) Count deletion requests received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(B) Count correction requests received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(C) Count know requests received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(D) Count requests to access automated decision-making technology received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(E) Count sale/sharing opt-out requests received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(F) Count requests to limit received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(G) Count automated decision-making opt-out requests received, fulfilled and denied. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(1)(H) Report median or mean days taken to respond substantively to requests. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(a)(2) Publish the metrics by July 1 yearly in or linked from privacy policy. Coming soon
11 CCR §7102(b) Metrics may cover all individuals; state this, and give the Attorney General consumer-only figures on request. Coming soon
11 CCR Art. 9 CYBERSECURITY AUDITS
11 CCR §7120 Requirement to Complete a Cybersecurity Audit.
11 CCR §7120(a) Businesses whose processing poses significant security risk must complete a cybersecurity audit. Coming soon
11 CCR §7120(b) Defines when processing counts as significant security risk.
11 CCR §7120(b)(1) Risk threshold met via the revenue-from-data-sales threshold in the Civil Code. Coming soon
11 CCR §7120(b)(2) Risk threshold met via the revenue-size threshold plus a volume condition.
11 CCR §7120(b)(2)(A) Volume condition: processed data of 250,000 or more consumers or households. Coming soon
11 CCR §7120(b)(2)(B) Volume condition: processed sensitive data of 50,000 or more consumers. Coming soon
11 CCR §7121 Timing Requirements for Cybersecurity Audits and Audit Reports.
11 CCR §7121(a) Sets deadlines for the first cybersecurity audit report.
11 CCR §7121(a)(1) Businesses over $100 million revenue: first report due April 1, 2028. Coming soon
11 CCR §7121(a)(2) Businesses with $50-100 million revenue: first report due April 1, 2029. Coming soon
11 CCR §7121(a)(3) Businesses under $50 million revenue: first report due April 1, 2030. Coming soon
11 CCR §7121(b) After 2030, qualifying businesses audit the following year and report by April 1 after. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122 Thoroughness and Independence of Cybersecurity Audits.
11 CCR §7122(a) Audits must use a qualified, objective, independent professional following accepted auditing standards.
11 CCR §7122(a)(1) Auditor must understand cybersecurity and how to audit a security program. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(a)(2) Auditor may be internal or external but must be impartial and not audit own work. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(a)(3) Internal auditor's head reports to an executive not running cybersecurity, who sets pay. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(b) Business must give the auditor all relevant information requested. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(c) Business must disclose relevant facts in good faith and not misstate any. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(d) Audit findings must rest mainly on evidence, not management assertions. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(e) Audit report must contain the content listed in section 7123(e). Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(f) Give the audit report to an executive directly responsible for cybersecurity. Coming soon
11 CCR §7122(g) Business and auditor keep audit documents for at least five years. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123 Scope of Cybersecurity Audit and Audit Report.
11 CCR §7123(a) Audit assesses protection of personal information against unauthorized access, change, destruction and loss of availability. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(b) Lists what the cybersecurity audit must assess.
11 CCR §7123(b)(1) Assess whether the cybersecurity program and its documentation are suitable for the business. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(b)(2) Assess each applicable program component listed in subsection (c). Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(b)(3) Assess how the business implements and enforces its cybersecurity program. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c) Lists program components the audit must assess where applicable.
11 CCR §7123(c)(1) Audit component: authentication.
11 CCR §7123(c)(1)(A) Audit component: multi-factor authentication, including phishing-resistant forms for personnel. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(1)(B) Audit component: strong, unique, non-reused passwords where passwords are used. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(2) Audit component: encrypting personal information stored and transmitted. We detect

db.sensitive-column-plaintextCard, ID or health data shows no encryption at rest.

tls.verification-disabledEncryption in transit without peer authentication is a deficiency an auditor records under this component.
11 CCR §7123(c)(3) Audit component: account management and access controls.
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(A) Audit component: limiting each person's, account's or application's access to what duties need. We detect

arch.privileged-key-client-sideThe client application holds privileges far beyond what it needs.

db.rls-missingAccounts reach all rows rather than only those they need.
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(A)(i) Limit personnel access to job needs and revoke it when no longer required. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(A)(ii) Limit service provider access to what their contract's business purposes require. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(A)(iii) Limit third-party access to data needed for contract-specified purposes. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(B) Audit component: minimising and tightly controlling privileged accounts, including just-in-time access tooling. We detect

arch.privileged-key-client-sideA privileged credential is usable by anyone, so its use is not restricted to necessary functions.
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(C) Audit component: restricting and monitoring creation of new accounts and their privileges. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(3)(D) Audit component: restricting and monitoring physical access to personal information. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(4) Audit component: inventory and management of personal information and information systems.
11 CCR §7123(c)(4)(A) Audit component: personal information inventories, data flow maps, classification and tagging. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(4)(B) Audit component: hardware and software inventories and allowlisting. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(4)(C) Audit component: approval of hardware and software; blocking unauthorized devices. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(5) Audit component: secure configuration of hardware and software. We detect

secrets.insecure-defaultThe application's shipped configuration presets its signing secret to a published sample, a gap in the secure-configuration component.
11 CCR §7123(c)(5)(A) Audit component: software updates and upgrades. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(5)(B) Audit component: securing on-premises and cloud environments. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(5)(C) Audit component: default masking of sensitive personal information in applications. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(5)(D) Audit component: security patch management, from notification through verified deployment. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(5)(E) Audit component: change management so changes do not weaken safeguards. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(6) Audit component: vulnerability scans, penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure programs. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(7) Audit component: audit-log management with centralized storage, retention and monitoring. We detect

db.audit-table-mutableAudit logs can be altered by application roles, so they are not managed securely.

db.audit-trail-missingChanges to sensitive and business records are not logged at all.

db.cascade-deletes-historyAudit and history records are deleted with the row instead of being retained.
11 CCR §7123(c)(8) Audit component: network monitoring and defenses.
11 CCR §7123(c)(8)(A) Audit component: bot, intrusion detection and prevention technologies. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(8)(B) Audit component: data-loss-prevention systems. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(9) Audit component: antivirus and antimalware protections. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(10) Audit component: segmenting the information system with firewalls, routers or switches. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(11) Audit component: limiting and controlling ports, services and protocols. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(12) Audit component: staying current on changing threats and countermeasures. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(13) Audit component: security training for all personnel with system access. Coming soon
11 CCR §7123(c)(14) Audit component: secure development practices, including code review and testing. We detect

ci.missingNo automated testing gate runs on changes, a gap in the secure-development component.

ci.nonblocking-checksTests and security checks cannot block a change, so testing is not enforced.

tests.no-coverage-floorTesting has no enforced coverage threshold.

Reuse: Official state legal text, free to read; reuse terms not checked; cite section numbers and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
